title: Nightly perf baseline runs: multi-region runner, artifact storage, and Slack summary diffs
author: Sahana Iyer
body:
Context: This PR wires the Q1'26 perf baseline suite into perf-canary as a nightly job. It runs the locked workload suite against the baseline model matrix across selected regions/hardware, stores structured artifacts, and posts a summary diff to Slack. This is the first step in the gate rollout plan (warn-only drift detection; no blocking yet).

What this adds:
- Nightly schedule (02:30 UTC) for `baseline-suite` with a separate "manual rerun" entrypoint.
- Multi-region execution: `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, `eu-west-1` fanout with a per-region concurrency cap and per-shape retry semantics.
- Artifact storage: per-run bundle uploaded to `s3://redwood-perf-canary/baselines/<run_id>/` including `summary.json`, `metrics.parquet`, `runner-metadata.json`, and logs. Each artifact is stamped with runtime build metadata (git SHA, docker image digest, driver/CUDA pins where present) so the run is reproducible.
- Slack summary diffs posted to `#eng-runtime-perf` with: run link, top regressions/improvements by metric (TTFT/TPOT/e2e p95/p99, throughput), and failure classification breakdown.
- Retry logic + failure classification: the runner distinguishes (a) infra/fleet issues (timeout, node preemption, env drift detected), (b) harness errors (schema/validation), (c) suspected regression (metric drift beyond variance budget), and (d) expected noise (within budget). Only (a)/(b) trigger automatic retries; (c) does not retry to avoid hiding real regressions.

Policy in this PR (warn-only):
- Nightly posts are informational; no paging.
- If >20% of shapes in a region fail as infra/fleet, post a separate "RUN UNHEALTHY" message and tag SRE-oncall (matches current draft runbook direction).

Implementation notes:
- Runner output schema is normalized to the baseline harness output (see `benchmark-lab` output JSON) and then converted to parquet for dashboards.
- Baseline comparison uses last "green" run per (model, region, hardware, traffic_shape) as the reference if the pinned baseline tag is missing. This avoids a total outage of diffing if one region misses a run.

Rollout plan:
1) Land this PR and run nightly for 1 week (warn-only) to measure variance and infra failure modes.
2) Add dashboards/alerts consuming the stored artifacts (separate PR in observability-pack).
3) Tighten retry policy + add explicit env-drift enforcement once INT-1440 is resolved.

Test plan:
- `make test` + unit tests for classification + diff ranking.
- `./cmd/perf-canary run baseline-suite --dry-run` against staging artifact bucket.
- Manual end-to-end run in `us-east-1` (run id: `pc_2026-02-09T1840Z_6f9c`).

Checklist:
- [x] Artifacts include run metadata stamping (commit/image/region/hw)
- [x] Slack messages include links to artifacts + dashboards placeholder
- [x] Failure classification is explicit and reported
- [x] Backoff + retry bounded (no infinite loops)
- [x] Docs updated for oncall reruns

Notes/risks:
- Env drift detection is best-effort right now (we record driver/CUDA from node labels where available). Full enforcement will follow once fleet normalization changes land.
- Slack diff output is capped to avoid spam (top 10 deltas per metric + failures summary).
commits: perf-canary: add baseline suite workflow and scheduler entrypoint
runner: implement multi-region fanout with concurrency cap and backoff
artifacts: upload summary/parquet/log bundles with metadata stamping
diff: compute baseline deltas and rank top changes by metric
slack: post nightly summary + unhealthy run notification
docs: add rerun instructions and failure classification glossary
conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): The failure categories look good, but I want to make sure we do NOT retry suspected regressions. Otherwise tail issues will get washed out. Also, tagging SRE-oncall should only happen for systemic failures; can we gate on >=20% shapes failing with infra classification per region? And please add a runbook link in the Slack message.

Sahana Iyer (author): Updated retry policy: only infra + harness errors retry; suspected regressions never retry. Added "unhealthy" threshold at 20% infra failures per region and included runbook link + artifact link in Slack payload.

Allison Grant (review): Artifact schema is fine, but please keep dimensions stable and avoid exploding cardinality. Do we really need per-request IDs in stored logs/metrics? Also confirm we’re not writing prompt text anywhere.

Sahana Iyer (author): Removed per-request IDs from parquet output (kept only aggregated histograms + counts). Confirmed prompts are synthetic / hashed IDs only; no raw prompt content is stored by perf-canary. Added explicit assertion in schema validation that `prompt_text` fields are absent.

Marcus Reed (review): Diffing behavior using "last green" is reasonable, but can you make the reference selection explicit in the summary.json? Otherwise it’s hard to interpret deltas. Also, please include benchmark harness version in metadata.
Sahana Iyer (author): Added `reference_run_id` + `reference_policy` to summary. Metadata now includes `workload_suite_version` + `harness_version` (from benchmark-lab tag) when available.
Sergio Costa (review): Slack output formatting: please cap long lists and include a compact table. Also include region/hardware in each delta line to reduce back-and-forth.
Sahana Iyer (author): Slack message now caps to top 10 per metric, uses a fixed-width block table, and includes (region, hw, traffic_shape) per row.

Connor O'Brien (review): For release qualification later, we’ll need the workflow to be reusable (manual trigger + parameters). Can we add workflow_dispatch with region override and baseline tag override?
Sahana Iyer (author): Added `workflow_dispatch` inputs for regions, baseline_tag, and max_parallel. Defaults remain the nightly config.
Sean Gallagher (final): Approved with the retry + unhealthy threshold changes. Please ensure docs/runbooks is discoverable from the oncall index (follow-up is fine).
Allison Grant (final): Approved. Thanks for removing per-request IDs and adding the no-prompt assertion.
